propositions: T5c security-review findings cite repo artifacts despite the as-written evaluation stance, indicating misalignment between the shared preamble and security-specific requirements.

Thirty percent of T5c advisories follow an undeclared-access-posture template shape that duplicates across multiple surfaces in the same plan, causing findings to displace other criteria in advisory-cap-limited reviews.
The rubric must be rewritten to ground findings in the current codebase and configuration rather than the spec-as-written, with controls defined elsewhere flipping findings.
Undeclared-access-posture findings must be capped at one per plan with extra surfaces folded into evidence (dedup-at-source) instead of one finding per surface.
Candidate findings citing neither a repo artifact nor a quoted plan sentence must be demoted to minor severity rather than suppressed, preserving ungrounded findings below the blocking threshold.
Only two HIGH-severity classes warrant priority >= major: plaintext secrets on boundary-crossing paths and undeclared internet-reachable sensitive surfaces; all other findings are at most minor.
